column1: # The gender of a crowd portrait: the soldier, the miko, the passer-by. Hand-
# written; this is the file to edit.
# Columns: the portrait key <TAB> the name its plate prints <TAB> the gender
# <TAB> where the answer came from. modules/PortraitGenders.js reads the first
# and the third; the other two are for whoever reads this next.
# Keyed by the portrait rather than by the plate's English name, which is the
# whole reason this file is not more rows in glossaries/character_genders.md.
# 汎用ゼス男魔法兵 and 汎用ゼス女魔法兵 are both "Zeth Mage Soldier" over the
# portrait, and so are 汎用男武士兵 and 汎用女武士兵 both "JAPAN Samurai" and all
# four ポピンズ both sexes of "Poppins". A table keyed by name has one row to
# give them and would be telling a translator the wrong pronoun for 819 lines.
# That other file stays a table of characters -- people with a name, a history
# and a wiki page. These are costumes. Nothing here belongs in a cast list, and
# a row here answering somebody that file also answers is a mistake rather than
# a fallback: scripts/extract_scenes.js asks the character table first and
# complains about any row here it never had to reach.
# The evidence is in the last column because it is not all of one kind, and the
# difference matters. 8_カードデータ.x has a 性別 column the game itself reads
# (modules/CardGenders.js), and where a card wears one of these costumes that is
# strong evidence -- but it is evidence about the card, not about the extra in
# the same outfit. 汎用自由都市警備兵Ａ dresses five 警備兵 cards that all say
# Female, and every line spoken from behind that portrait is a man's: 「なんで俺
# までっ！？」, 「女性の方もかなり好きモノですなあ」. So the lines win where the two
# disagree, and that row says so out loud.
# 汎用その他 is the one honest "?". It is the game's own junk drawer: a Hanny
# saying はにはに in one scene and a crowd of men fighting over who gets to
# father Wenlina's child in another. Listed rather than left out, so the next
# person to look does not have to find that out again.
# A portrait not in this file and not in character_genders.md gets "?" on the
# cast line, which is the honest answer and the useless one. `node
# scripts/find_gender_gaps.js` is the list of those.
